findings.issue_text: Double interpolation of queries in shard-splitting path: queries are interpolated once at top of runShardSplitQuery and again inside splitQueriesByStreamShard, and template interpolation is not idempotent so second pass can corrupt queries (P1)

runSplitQuery may have the same double-interpolation problem: newly added up-front interpolation may compound with interpolation inside the chunking path, and the test only checks the first runQuery call's expr so it would go unnoticed (P2)

Mutating request.targets via applyTemplateVariables: mapping over request.targets and passing targets to applyTemplateVariables may mutate the originals with interpolated expressions, breaking re-interpolation on refresh/variable-change and confusing downstream consumers like query history and change detection (P2)

P3: Repeated template interpolation per shard group — the refactor moved from a single batched interpolateVariablesInQueries call to per-query datasource.applyTemplateVariables calls, and interpolated queries are re-interpolated again per shard group in splitQueriesByStreamShard, growing interpolation work from O(targets) to O(targets × shardGroups) (shardQuerySplitting.ts:~109)

Test mocks for applyTemplateVariables mutate the input query object in place (query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)), suggesting the real implementation may also mutate request.targets entries, which could introduce correctness bugs via shared mutable state across split queries

Possible double interpolation / premature $__auto resolution when runSplitQuery is called from the normal query path: query() already interpolates targets, and applyTemplateVariables inside runSplitQuery causes a second interpolation that may bake in a per-chunk interval value that doesn't match splitting logic (public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:293-299)

applyTemplateVariables is now invoked on raw target objects instead of interpolateVariablesInQueries, changing semantics; it is called repeatedly per shard group (5 times for one logical query), causing re-interpolation of already-interpolated queries, and external callers stubbing interpolateVariablesInQueries silently lose effect (public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52 and querySplitting.ts:296-297)

Hidden/non-expr queries are no longer interpolated in the shard path because filtering by expr/hide now happens before interpolation; those targets may pass through uninterpolated to runQuery or other consumers (public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52)

P2: applyTemplateVariables mutates request.targets query objects in place, so reused requests on refresh/retry lose raw template expressions and produce stale/garbled results (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-51)
P3: applyTemplateVariables throwing synchronously inside .map() escapes the observable contract, bypassing panel-level error handling (querySplitting.ts:296, shardQuerySplitting.ts:51)

Splitting decisions now run on interpolated queries instead of raw ones — applyTemplateVariables runs before partitioning/splitting, so interpolated expressions (regex special chars, resolved ranges/$__auto) can change splitting outcomes, with no test pinning the behavior (regression risk)

Test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts only mock call counts (toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)) and expect.any(...) args, not actual behavior — repeated per-query interpolation (possible double-interpolation corrupting literal '$' or regex like ~"$var") is unverified

Test mock of applyTemplateVariables mutates the query in place and only mirrors the expr field, differing from production semantics (returns new object, handles step/filters) — the mutation-based mock could hide bugs like dropped mapped results

Missing edge-case tests: applyTemplateVariables throwing on uninterpolatable queries (could now break the whole request), queries whose expr becomes empty/invalid after interpolation, and hidden/expr-less targets combined with the new .map() ordering

applyTemplateVariables now receives request.filters (old interpolateVariablesInQueries path did not) — ad-hoc filters may be applied or double-applied to split shard queries, with no test covering the filters path

Filter-before-interpolate ordering regression: queries whose expr is entirely a template variable that resolves to empty (e.g. "${unused_var}") are no longer filtered out after interpolation, letting empty-expr queries through to splitQueriesByStreamShard/runQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52, querySplitting.ts:295-298)

Interpolation is applied repeatedly in shard splitting (once per shard group/batch) and double-applied in runSplitQuery since runQuery applies applyTemplateVariables again, which can mangle variable values or log-line filters containing literal '$' (shardQuerySplitting.ts:46-52, querySplitting.ts:293-298)

In-place mutation of request targets by applyTemplateVariables is now load-bearing: if datasource implementations mutate the query object, request.targets is corrupted for downstream consumers like retries or refreshes, re-interpolating already-interpolated text (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52)
querySupportsSplitting/isLogsQuery in runSplitQuery now run against interpolated text, changing classification behavior for exprs whose structure changes under interpolation

goldens.comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

The candidate expands on potential consequences (double-application), but the core issue of passing filters without corresponding test coverage matches the golden concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double interpolation of queries in shard-splitting path: queries are interpolated once at top of runShardSplitQuery and again inside splitQueriesByStreamShard, and template interpolation is not idempotent so second pass can corrupt queries (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates upfront via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` (shardQuerySplitting.ts). The updated test `Interpolates queries before running` now expects `applyTemplateVariables` to have been called 5 times even though there is only 1 target, implying additional interpolation happens later in the shard-splitting path (likely inside `splitQueriesByStreamShard`, though that function isn’t shown in this diff). This supports the “multiple interpolation passes” concern, but the claim that a second pass is non-idempotent and can “corrupt queries (P1)” is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: runSplitQuery may have the same double-interpolation problem: newly added up-front interpolation may compound with interpolation inside the chunking path, and the test only checks the first runQuery call's expr so it would go unnoticed (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `runSplitQuery` the diff adds an up-front `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` before any splitting/chunking. The new test `Interpolates queries before execution` only inspects `datasource.runQuery.mock.calls[0][0]...`, i.e., the first `runQuery` invocation, so it would not catch if later `runQuery` calls (e.g., for subsequent chunks) re-apply template interpolation or otherwise differ. The claimed “double-interpolation” itself isn’t directly verifiable from this diff (no later interpolation shown), but the limited assertion scope in the test is grounded and could mask such an issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutating request.targets via applyTemplateVariables: mapping over request.targets and passing targets to applyTemplateVariables may mutate the originals with interpolated expressions, breaking re-interpolation on refresh/variable-change and confusing downstream consumers like query history and change detection (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...)` directly on objects from `request.targets` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...))` without cloning. If `applyTemplateVariables` mutates its input (as the updated tests’ mocks do by assigning `query.expr = ...`), this would mutate `request.targets` in-place, which can create subtle state/caching issues across refreshes or downstream consumers expecting the original targets. The diff alone doesn’t prove the real implementation mutates, but it does introduce/enable this risk by passing original target objects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Repeated template interpolation per shard group — the refactor moved from a single batched interpolateVariablesInQueries call to per-query datasource.applyTemplateVariables calls, and interpolated queries are re-interpolated again per shard group in splitQueriesByStreamShard, growing interpolation work from O(targets) to O(targets × shardGroups) (shardQuerySplitting.ts:~109)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows runShardSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables per query via a .map(...) instead of a single interpolateVariablesInQueries call. Additionally, the updated test now expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times even though the request has a single target, implying applyTemplateVariables is being invoked again during shard splitting (outside the initial map). This supports the finding’s performance concern about repeated interpolation work increasing beyond O(targets). It’s a concrete efficiency/architecture regression, not a correctness bug, but the exact location (~109) can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test mocks for applyTemplateVariables mutate the input query object in place (query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)), suggesting the real implementation may also mutate request.targets entries, which could introduce correctness bugs via shared mutable state across split queries

adjudication.rationale: In the updated tests, the mock `applyTemplateVariables` implementations mutate the passed-in `LokiQuery` object in place (`query.expr = ...; return query;`). In the production changes, both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` now pass the original `request.targets` objects directly into `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` via `.map(...)` without cloning. While the diff does not prove the real `applyTemplateVariables` mutates, the API usage makes in-place mutation of `request.targets` possible and the tests model that behavior, which could be a shared-mutable-state risk across later query processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Possible double interpolation / premature $__auto resolution when runSplitQuery is called from the normal query path: query() already interpolates targets, and applyTemplateVariables inside runSplitQuery causes a second interpolation that may bake in a per-chunk interval value that doesn't match splitting logic (public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:293-299)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` inside both `runSplitQuery` (querySplitting.ts:293-299) and `runShardSplitQuery` (shardQuerySplitting.ts:46-55), meaning these helpers now always perform interpolation on the targets they receive. The finding’s concern (double interpolation / prematurely resolving `$__auto` if an upstream normal query path already interpolates before calling these helpers) is a concrete architectural/behavior risk introduced by this change, but the diff does not show the upstream `query()` path or whether it already interpolates targets, so an actual defect cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: applyTemplateVariables is now invoked on raw target objects instead of interpolateVariablesInQueries, changing semantics; it is called repeatedly per shard group (5 times for one logical query), causing re-interpolation of already-interpolated queries, and external callers stubbing interpolateVariablesInQueries silently lose effect (public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52 and querySplitting.ts:296-297)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a switch from `interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, ...)` to mapping `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`, so stubs of `interpolateVariablesInQueries` would no longer apply. However, the finding’s core claim that `applyTemplateVariables` is “called repeatedly per shard group (5 times for one logical query), causing re-interpolation of already-interpolated queries” is not verifiable from the shown code: `runShardSplitQuery` only maps over the filtered targets once, and no repeated interpolation per shard group is shown in this diff. Any additional calls would have to be inside `splitQueriesByStreamShard` or elsewhere, which is not part of the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hidden/non-expr queries are no longer interpolated in the shard path because filtering by expr/hide now happens before interpolation; those targets may pass through uninterpolated to runQuery or other consumers (public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52)

adjudication.rationale: In runShardSplitQuery, targets are now filtered by `query.expr` and `!query.hide` before being mapped through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)`. Hidden or non-expr targets are excluded from the `queries` array entirely, so they cannot “pass through uninterpolated to runQuery or other consumers” within this shard-splitting path. Previously, interpolation happened before filtering, but those filtered-out targets still would not have been used downstream.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: applyTemplateVariables mutates request.targets query objects in place, so reused requests on refresh/retry lose raw template expressions and produce stale/garbled results (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-51)

adjudication.rationale: In both runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery the diff now passes each LokiQuery object from request.targets directly into datasource.applyTemplateVariables via .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...)). The diff does not show whether applyTemplateVariables clones or mutates, but the updated tests mock it by mutating query.expr in place and returning the same object. If the real implementation also mutates, this could indeed modify request.targets for the caller and affect reuse of the same request object. However, the mutation behavior itself is not verifiable from this diff alone, so it’s a concrete risk/concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: applyTemplateVariables throwing synchronously inside .map() escapes the observable contract, bypassing panel-level error handling (querySplitting.ts:296, shardQuerySplitting.ts:51)

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves template interpolation into a synchronous `.map(...)` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` (`.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`). If `applyTemplateVariables` can throw, that exception will occur before any observable is returned/emitted, meaning it won’t be represented as an `error` notification in whatever Rx pipeline wraps the query execution. However, the diff alone doesn’t show the surrounding observable contract/panel error handling to prove it’s a user-visible defect; it’s a plausible robustness/architecture concern grounded in the new synchronous mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Splitting decisions now run on interpolated queries instead of raw ones — applyTemplateVariables runs before partitioning/splitting, so interpolated expressions (regex special chars, resolved ranges/$__auto) can change splitting outcomes, with no test pinning the behavior (regression risk)

adjudication.rationale: It is true that both runSplitQuery() and runShardSplitQuery() now call datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...) before partitioning/splitting (querySplitting.ts maps before partition; shardQuerySplitting.ts maps after filtering). However, the finding claims there is “no test pinning the behavior”, which is contradicted by the diff: new tests explicitly assert that interpolation happens before execution and that the resulting expr/step passed to datasource.runQuery are interpolated (querySplitting.test.ts new test; shardQuerySplitting.test.ts new test), and an existing shard test was updated to assert applyTemplateVariables call count. The claimed untested regression risk is therefore not supported by the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts only mock call counts (toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)) and expect.any(...) args, not actual behavior — repeated per-query interpolation (possible double-interpolation corrupting literal '$' or regex like ~"$var") is unverified

adjudication.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.test.ts, the existing test "Interpolates queries before running" was updated to `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` and the subsequent `runQuery` assertion uses broad matchers like `expect.any(Number)` rather than checking the interpolated query content. Given the diff changes from a single `interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)` call to per-query `applyTemplateVariables(...)` (runShardSplitQuery now maps `request.targets` through `applyTemplateVariables`), the test does not directly verify that repeated/per-query interpolation produces the correct final `expr`/`step` for those multiple calls (e.g., guarding against unintended repeated interpolation effects). This is a test quality/coverage concern, not a demonstrable functional bug from the diff alone, especially since new tests were added that verify at least one interpolated execution path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test mock of applyTemplateVariables mutates the query in place and only mirrors the expr field, differing from production semantics (returns new object, handles step/filters) — the mutation-based mock could hide bugs like dropped mapped results

Missing edge-case tests: applyTemplateVariables throwing on uninterpolatable queries (could now break the whole request), queries whose expr becomes empty/invalid after interpolation, and hidden/expr-less targets combined with the new .map() ordering

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new behavior where `applyTemplateVariables` is invoked per-target via `.map(...)` after filtering (`runSplitQuery`: filters then `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`; `runShardSplitQuery`: same). This adds nontrivial interpolation logic in the execution path, but the added tests only cover successful interpolation. The finding’s proposed edge cases are diff-grounded: if `applyTemplateVariables` throws, it would now fail the whole request; and because filtering for `query.expr` happens *before* interpolation, a query whose `expr` becomes empty/invalid after interpolation would still be included (not re-filtered). These are specific missing tests around the newly added `.map` usage and ordering, not a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: applyTemplateVariables now receives request.filters (old interpolateVariablesInQueries path did not) — ad-hoc filters may be applied or double-applied to split shard queries, with no test covering the filters path
matched_golden_ids: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that applyTemplateVariables is now being called with request.filters and that the filters-related behavior is not covered/validated by existing tests. The candidate expands on potential consequences (double-application), but the core issue of passing filters without corresponding test coverage matches the golden concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Filter-before-interpolate ordering regression: queries whose expr is entirely a template variable that resolves to empty (e.g. "${unused_var}") are no longer filtered out after interpolation, letting empty-expr queries through to splitQueriesByStreamShard/runQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52, querySplitting.ts:295-298)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes both runSplitQuery() and runShardSplitQuery() to filter targets by `query.expr` *before* calling `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` (querySplitting.ts: now `.filter((q)=>q.expr)... .map(applyTemplateVariables)`, shardQuerySplitting.ts: now `.filter((q)=>q.expr)... .map(applyTemplateVariables)`). If a target’s `expr` is a non-empty template (e.g. "$unused") that interpolates to an empty string, it will pass the pre-interpolation filter and there is no post-interpolation filter to remove it, so an empty `expr` can reach downstream splitting/runQuery logic. Previously shardQuerySplitting interpolated first and then filtered by `expr`, so this is a regression in ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Interpolation is applied repeatedly in shard splitting (once per shard group/batch) and double-applied in runSplitQuery since runQuery applies applyTemplateVariables again, which can mangle variable values or log-line filters containing literal '$' (shardQuerySplitting.ts:46-52, querySplitting.ts:293-298)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, both runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts:293-298) and runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:46-52) apply datasource.applyTemplateVariables exactly once per non-hidden target via a single .map() before any splitting logic. The diff does not show datasource.runQuery applying applyTemplateVariables again, nor does it show interpolation being re-applied per shard group/batch. Therefore the claim of repeated/double interpolation cannot be verified from the provided changes and mischaracterizes what is visible here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place mutation of request targets by applyTemplateVariables is now load-bearing: if datasource implementations mutate the query object, request.targets is corrupted for downstream consumers like retries or refreshes, re-interpolating already-interpolated text (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52)

adjudication.rationale: In `runShardSplitQuery` the code now does `request.targets...map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...))` (shardQuerySplitting.ts). This passes the original target objects directly into `applyTemplateVariables` without cloning. The updated tests mock `applyTemplateVariables` by mutating `query.expr` in-place and returning the same object, which demonstrates that in-place mutation is plausible. Whether this actually causes downstream breakage (retries/refreshes/double-interpolation) isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, but the change does introduce a concrete risk of mutating `request.targets`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: querySupportsSplitting/isLogsQuery in runSplitQuery now run against interpolated text, changing classification behavior for exprs whose structure changes under interpolation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `runSplitQuery` to call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on each target before `partition(...)` uses `querySupportsSplitting(query)` and `isLogsQuery(query.expr)`. This means splitting/log-vs-metric classification is now based on the interpolated `expr` instead of the raw template text, which can change behavior when variables expand into different query structures. The finding is accurate and is a noteworthy behavior change, but the diff (and added tests asserting interpolation before execution) suggests this is intentional rather than a clear defect.
